- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.67) in recent days, model tends to underreact — increase forecast slightly to align with bullish momentum.  
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ 0.33) or shows sharp drops, model often overcorrects downward — adjust upward to avoid excessive pessimism.  
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >10% from prior peak), model frequently overshoots and fails to correct — reduce forecast slope after peak to reflect mean reversion.  
- If true outcome shows strong divergence from forecast in first 5–7 days (e.g., >5% deviation), model is lagging — apply early correction bias toward true direction.  
- Model consistently underestimates true price peaks in 30-day horizon — add 2–3% buffer to forecast when sentiment is bullish or volatility is high.  
- When sentiment history shows alternating highs/lows (e.g., 0.67 → 0.00 → 1.00), model often misreads trend — use sentiment-weighted average to smooth forecast.  
- If true outcome is below forecast for 3+ consecutive days, model is overconfident — reduce forecast slope or add downward bias to reflect mean reversion.
